--- title: "Extraction Pipeline" description: "Explore entity extraction backends — structured (batched), legacy (text parsing), and GLiNER — plus quality modes and fallback behavior." date: today format: html: self-contained: true embed-resources: true code-fold: true code-tools: true --- ## Introduction Entity extraction is the core of nano-graphrag's indexing pipeline. It reads text chunks and produces a structured knowledge graph of entities and relationships. nano-graphrag supports three extraction backends: | Backend | How it Works | Quality | Speed | Cost | |---------|-------------|---------|-------|------| | **Structured** (default) | LLM returns Pydantic JSON via structured output | High | Medium | Higher | | **Legacy** | LLM returns text, parsed with regex/delimiters | Medium | Medium | Higher | | **GLiNER** | Local neural model, no LLM calls | Medium | Fast | Free | Additionally, there are two **quality modes** that control LLM model selection and gleaning: - **`balanced`** (default): Uses the main LLM model with gleaning (follow-up prompts to refine extraction) - **`fast`**: Uses the cheap LLM model, no gleaning, larger batch sizes This notebook demonstrates each backend and quality mode, and explains the fallback chain. ## Setup ::: {#setup .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import logging import time from pathlib import Path logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING) logging.getLogger("nano-graphrag").setLevel(logging.INFO) TEXT_SNIPPET = ( "Alice works at Wonderland Labs as a quantum researcher. " "Bob is the CTO of Wonderland Labs and oversees the AI division. " "Carol founded DataForge, a startup building graph databases. " "Dave joined DataForge as lead engineer after leaving CloudCorp. " "Eve is a security consultant who audits both Wonderland Labs and DataForge." ) ``` ::: ::: {#imports .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from nano_graphrag import GraphRAG, QueryParam ``` ::: ## 1. Structured Extraction (Default) When `structured_output=True` (the default) and the model supports structured output, nano-graphrag uses the **structured extraction pipeline**. The LLM is asked to return a JSON object conforming to a Pydantic schema, and results are parsed directly — no regex needed. **How it works:** 1. Chunks are grouped into batches (default: `extraction_batch_size=5`) 2. Each batch is sent as a single LLM call with multiple numbered chunks 3. The LLM returns a `BatchedEntityExtractionOutput` with entities and relationships per chunk 4. Results are parsed via Pydantic validation — no text parsing ::: {#structured-default .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} WORKING_DIR_STRUCT = Path("./_cache/05_extraction_pipeline/structured") WORKING_DIR_STRUCT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) rag_structured = GraphRAG( working_dir=str(WORKING_DIR_STRUCT), structured_output=True, extraction_batch_size=5, ) print(f"Extraction: structured (batch_size={rag_structured.extraction_batch_size})") print(f"Use structured extraction: {rag_structured._use_structured_extraction}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

Good for small models or complex text. - `batch_size=3-5`: Good balance. Default is 5. - `batch_size=8+`: Best throughput but needs models with 32K+ token context. Auto-used in `fast` mode. ## 5. Concurrency Control Two settings control parallelism: - `extraction_max_async` — max concurrent LLM calls for chunk extraction (default: 16) - `doc_extraction_max_async` — max concurrent documents being processed (default: 4) ::: {#concurrency-demo .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} WORKING_DIR_CONC = Path("./_cache/05_extraction_pipeline/concurrency") WORKING_DIR_CONC.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) rag_conc = GraphRAG( working_dir=str(WORKING_DIR_CONC), extraction_max_async=8, doc_extraction_max_async=2, ) print(f"Chunk-level concurrency: {rag_conc.extraction_max_async}") print(f"Doc-level concurrency: {rag_conc.doc_extraction_max_async}") print() print("Max concurrent LLM calls = chunk_concurrency × doc_concurrency") print(f"Peak: {rag_conc.extraction_max_async} × {rag_conc.doc_extraction_max_async} = {rag_conc.extraction_max_async * rag_conc.doc_extraction_max_async}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

GLiNER Backend (Configuration) The GLiNER backend uses a local neural model (no LLM API calls) for entity extraction.
